To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

TDP-43, a protein that accumulates in the brains of AD patients, accumulates in the brain of an AD animal model and that the levels of this protein are linked to the levels of Aβ oligomers in the brain.
TDP-43, a protein that is involved in neurodegeneration, accumulates in a mouse model for Alzheimer disease and its levels correlate with the levels Aβ oligomers.
TDP-43 is increased in the 5xFAD mouse model of Alzheimer's disease and that this increase correlates with Aβ oligomers levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of TDP43 in AD and the relation between Aβ and TDP- 43 in AD.
the study of TDP- 43 levels in the 3xTg-AD mouse model and their correlation with Aβ oligomer levels.
the identification of novel molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of AD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Aβ oligomers are a major contributor to TDP-43 changes in the 3xTg-AD mouse model of AD.
Aβ oligomers are a cause of TDP- 43 accumulation in 3×T-AD mice.
the levels of the C-terminal fragment of TDP- 43 correlate with Aβ oligomers in AD mice, and that Aβ oligomers may be a key factor in the accumulation of this TDP-43 fragment in AD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 3×TG-AD mice show an increase in soluble Aβ oligomer levels, and this increase correlates with an increase in TDP-42 levels.

Aβ oligomers are linked to TDP-43 accumulation in the brain of the 3× Tg-AD mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Aβ oligomers may be involved in TDP-42 pathology in AD and that TDP-43 may be a useful marker of the presence of toxic Aβ oligomers.
